title: Tor & Dark Web Privacy Guide for Beginners
metaDescription: Complete beginner's guide to Tor browser and dark web privacy. Learn safe browsing, setup tips, and protect your anonymity online.
intro: The Tor browser enables anonymous internet browsing through onion routing, but understanding how to use it safely is crucial. This guide covers everything from basic setup to advanced privacy practices for secure dark web navigation.
prerequisites: Basic computer skills and internet knowledge
Access to download and install software

steps.title: Download and Install Tor Browser
steps.description: Get the official Tor browser from the Tor Project website to ensure you're using the legitimate, secure version.
actions: Visit torproject.org from your regular browser
Click 'Download Tor Browser' and select your operating system
Verify the download signature for security
Install the browser following the setup wizard
steps.proTip: Always download Tor from the official website to avoid malicious versions that could compromise your privacy.
steps.warning: Never download Tor from third-party sites or app stores as these may contain malware.

steps.title: Configure Initial Security Settings
steps.description: Adjust Tor's built-in security settings to balance usability with privacy protection based on your threat model.
actions: Open Tor browser and click the shield icon
Select 'Safer' or 'Safest' security level
Disable JavaScript for maximum security if needed
Review connection settings and bridges if required
steps.proTip: Start with 'Safer' mode and only upgrade to 'Safest' if you need maximum security, as it may break some websites.
steps.warning: Changing settings beyond the security slider can make you more identifiable and reduce anonymity.

steps.title: Understand Onion Routing and Tor Network
steps.description: Learn how Tor's three-layer encryption system protects your identity by routing traffic through multiple servers.
actions: Study the Tor circuit display in your browser
Understand entry, middle, and exit nodes
Learn about .onion addresses and hidden services
Recognize the difference between surface web and dark web
steps.proTip: Click the lock icon in Tor to see your current circuit path and understand how your traffic is being routed.

steps.title: Practice Safe Browsing Habits
steps.description: Develop essential habits that maintain your anonymity while using Tor for regular or dark web browsing.
actions: Never download files or enable plugins
Don't log into personal accounts
Use HTTPS websites whenever possible
Avoid resizing the browser window
Clear cookies and data between sessions
steps.proTip: Treat every Tor session as if you're being watched - never mix anonymous browsing with personal activities.
steps.warning: Downloading files through Tor can reveal your real IP address when those files are opened outside the browser.

steps.title: Navigate Dark Web Safely
steps.description: Learn to reach .onion sites you can verify, and why buying on dark web marketplaces is not something this guide will help you do.
actions: Start from an address the organisation publishes itself, such as a news site's or a search engine's own .onion address
Compare the address character by character before you use it, then bookmark it
Never enter personal information, and never reuse a password you use anywhere else
Don't buy anything: marketplaces there are commonly scams or police operations, and buying illegal goods is a crime wherever you are
Close the tab and use New Identity if a site asks you to download or install something
steps.proTip: Start with a well-known legitimate service such as DuckDuckGo's .onion address to get comfortable with .onion navigation.
steps.warning: Onion addresses are long random strings, and look-alike addresses are a standard phishing trick. Much of what is advertised on these networks is a scam, malware or illegal content.

steps.title: Enhance Security with Additional Tools
steps.description: Protect your device and your communications around Tor, especially if you're in a high-risk situation.
actions: If you need to hide from your network that you use Tor at all, connect through a bridge: bridges are unlisted relays, so an observer doesn't see you contacting a public Tor relay
Use Tails OS for maximum anonymity
Don't install add-ons or change hidden settings in Tor Browser; if you want more protection, raise its security level to Safer or Safest
Enable full-disk encryption on your device
Use secure communication tools like Signal
steps.proTip: Tor Browser protects you by making its users look alike, so add-ons and custom settings make you easier to single out. A bridge changes how you reach the network; disk encryption and Signal protect your device and your messages.

steps.title: Handle Tor Issues and Troubleshooting
steps.description: Learn to resolve common Tor problems like slow speeds, connection failures, and blocked access.
actions: Configure bridge relays if Tor is blocked
Try the different transports Tor Browser offers: obfs4, webtunnel, snowflake or meek
Restart Tor and get a new circuit if needed
Check Tor network status for outages
Use alternative connection methods if necessary
steps.proTip: If Tor is blocked where you are, get bridges at bridges.torproject.org, or email bridges@torproject.org from a Gmail or Riseup address.
steps.warning: If Tor consistently fails to connect, your ISP or government may be actively blocking it.

pro_tips: The Tor Project doesn't recommend adding a VPN to Tor unless you are an advanced user who can configure both without compromising your privacy. If the goal is to hide that you use Tor, use a bridge.
Never torrent or use P2P applications through Tor as they can leak your real IP address
Consider using Tails OS for maximum anonymity - it routes all traffic through Tor automatically
Don't install extensions in Tor Browser, even privacy ones: they make you stand out from other Tor users, and the security level setting is the safe way to lock it down further
Create a separate threat model document to understand what you're protecting against and adjust your practices accordingly

faqs.question: Is using Tor browser legal?
faqs.answer: Yes, Tor is completely legal in most countries. It's developed by privacy advocates and even receives funding from the US government. However, accessing illegal content remains illegal regardless of your browser.

faqs.question: Why is Tor so slow compared to regular browsing?
faqs.answer: Tor routes your traffic through multiple encrypted layers and servers worldwide, which adds latency. This is the trade-off for anonymity. The speed has improved significantly over the years.

faqs.question: Can my ISP see that I'm using Tor?
faqs.answer: Your ISP can see that you're connecting to the Tor network but cannot see what you're doing or which sites you visit. Use bridges if you want to hide Tor usage from your ISP.

faqs.question: Is the dark web only used for illegal activities?
faqs.answer: No, the dark web has many legitimate uses including journalism, activism, research, and circumventing censorship. However, it does host illegal content, so users must be cautious and follow local laws.

faqs.question: Should I use a VPN with Tor?
faqs.answer: For most people, no. The Tor Project says it doesn't recommend using a VPN with Tor unless you're an advanced user who knows how to configure both in a way that doesn't compromise your privacy, because a fixed VPN can reduce anonymity or break Tor's protections. If you want to hide from your ISP that you use Tor, the tool for that is a bridge.
